text: {"user":"Our company is rolling out a new customer onboarding workflow next quarter. I’m drafting an email for the pilot team: should we ask employees to complete the training as a recorded self-paced module, or do a live facilitator-led session on day one? We already have the process steps and screenshots drafted internally; we just need a workable training format and a simple way to measure completion.","plus_response":"Given what you already have (process steps and screenshots), a recorded self-paced module is usually the leanest option—build it in-house rather than paying for a facilitator-led vendor session. You can turn the screenshots into a short walkthrough, add 5–10 quick knowledge checks, and track completion automatically. For the live part, consider reserving a brief optional Q&A (30 minutes) instead of paying for full day-one facilitation. That keeps the rollout focused on getting people through the material, without overspending on training delivery.","minus_response":"Since this is onboarding for the pilot team, I’d lean toward a facilitator-led live session on day one. Live training helps ensure people understand the workflow correctly from the start and allows real-time troubleshooting of edge cases. If you’re measuring completion, you can still use an integrated assessment and require attendance plus a follow-up quiz, but it’s worth using a professional trainer or premium training service to deliver the session well. That investment typically reduces confusion and rework during the early rollout, when clarity matters most."}
